box.highlights: Whitman 42, Longwood 0: Nicholas Bottoni passed for 230 yards and three touchdowns and rushed for a 10-yard score to lead Whitman (1-0) over host Longwood in Suffolk Division I. Bottoni connected with Tyriek Mays-Mckoy for touchdowns of 87 and 48 yards and with Rasahn Thompson on a 20-yarder. Thompson also had a 60-yard punt return for a touchdown and a 14-yard TD run. Liam Villanti had four tackles for a loss and Brandon Ivy and Chris Silverio each had an interception for the Wildcats. Najee Henderson had an interception for the Lions (0-1).

Whitman 34, Sachem North 14: Nicholas Bottoni completed 20 of 24 passes for 262 yards and three touchdowns and Brandon Ivy had six receptions for 106 yards and two touchdowns to lead Whitman (2-0) in Suffolk I. Jacob Somer had a strip-sack near the end of the second quarter and recovered the fumble to set up Tyriek Mays-Mckoy's 10-yard touchdown run to put Whitman up 21-0 going in halftime. AJ Evans had 115 yards and a touchdown on 11 carries and Jonathan Maldanado had 73 yards on seven carries. Mays-Mckoy had four catches for 47 yards and an interception. Luke Kannavos led the defense with eight tackles and a sack.

Whitman 35, Sachem East 14: Nicholas Bottoni completed 14 of 19 passes for 150 yards and a touchdown to lead Whitman (3-0) in Suffolk I. AJ Evans ran for 100 yards and a touchdown on 12 carries, Jonathan Maldonado had 63 yards and two touchdowns on 12 carries and Chris Silverio had four catches for 59 yards. Tyriek Mays-McKoy caught five passes for 50 yards and had 12 tackes, including five for a loss, and two sacks. Liam Villanti added 10 tackles and a sack.
Whitman 27, Floyd 0: Nick Bottoni threw three touchdowns and ran for another to lead Whitman (4-0) in Suffolk I.

Whitman 48, Bay Shore 0: Tyriek Mays-Mckoy had a 13-yard fumble recovery return for a score and a 20-yard punt return for a touchdown on back-to-back series for Whitman (5-0) in Suffolk I. The Wildcats had four defensive touchdowns. Rasahn Thompson and Brandon Ivy each had interception returns for touchdowns of 41 and 32 yards respectively. AJ Evans had rushing touchdowns of 5 and 21 yards, Cameron Carlson added a 5-yard rushing touchdown and seven tackles and Joe Gervasio had four tackles for a loss.

Whitman 41, Ward Melville 35: Nicholas Bottoni threw for 101 yards and two touchdowns on 6-of-7 passing in Suffolk I. His 29-yard pass to Tyriek Mays-McKoy in the fourth quarter gave Whitman a 41-28 lead. A.J Evans rushed for 123 yards and three touchdowns on 12 carries. He rushed for touchdowns of 7, 33, and 25 yards. Jonathan Maldonado ran for 59 yards and a touchdown. Mays-McKoy caught three passes for 43 yards and the winning touchdown. Ward Melville's Chris Prussen scored five touchdown, rushing for three and throwing for two. It is the first time Whitman had started 6-0 in the 83-year history of the program, according to Newsday records. Ward Melville is 4-2.

Whitman 34, Commack 14: Nicholas Bottoni threw for 305 yards and three touchdowns on 13-of-20 passing in Suffolk I Saturday. Brandon Ivy made seven catches for 176 yards and two touchdowns. Tyriek Mays-Mckoy had four catches for 93 yards and a touchdown. His 31-yard touchdown catch in the first quarter gave Whitman a 7-0 lead after an extra point. Whitman opened up a 27-7 lead after three quarters. Luke Kannavos made 11 tacks and had two sacks to lead Whitman (7-0). Commack is 5-2.

Whitman 36, Patchogue-Medford 6: Nicholas Bottoni completed 11 of 13 passes for 212 yards and three TDs and added a touchdown run to lead Whitman (8-0) in Suffolk I. Tyriek Mays-Mckoy had five catches for 145 yards and two TDs, including a one-handed 57-yard grab to open the second half. Mays-Mckoy also had a sack, a forced fumble and an interception. AJ Evans rushed for 116 yards and a touchdown on 20 carries, Liam Villanti had four tackles for loss, including two sacks, and a forced fumble, Brandon Ivy had an interception, and Joe Gervasio had a fumble recovery and a tackle in the end zone for a safety. Mikey Phillips had three catches for 44 yards and a touchdown. It was Whitman's first undefeated regular-season in program history, according to Ralph Milazzo.

Whitman 48, Riverhead 0: Nicholas Bottoni completed 7 of 7 passes for 210 yards and three touchdowns to lead No. 1 Whitman over No. 8 Riverhead in a Suffolk I quarterfinal. Mikey Phillips caught two passes for 62 yards and two touchdowns, AJ Evans had 78 yards and two touchdowns on seven carries and JD Harrison added 72 yards and a touchdown on eight carries. Jacob Somer had eight tackles, including three for a loss and Diego Romero had four tackles for a loss and forced a fumble. Whitman (9-0) scored on its first five possessions in the first quarter. The Wildcats will play Ward Melville in a semifinal.

Whitman 42, Floyd 7: Nicholas Bottoni threw for 205 yards and three touchdowns to lead No. 1 Whitman over No. 2 Floyd in the Suffolk I championship game. Bottoni connected with Tyriek Mays-Mckoy for a 33-yard touchdown in the first quarter and a 46-yard score in the third quarter. Mays-Mckoy finished with seven receptions for 171 yards. AJ Evans rushed for 81 yards and three touchdowns. This is the first Suffolk title for the Wildcats since 1984.  Whitman (11-0) will face Massapequa (10-1) on Friday at 12 p.m. in the Long Island Class I championship.
